newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia needs 4.0 to 4.5 pct growth - Howard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia needs 4.0 to 4.5 pct growth - Howard.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said the economy needed to grow at 4.0 to 4.5 percent a year, well above its long-term trend rate near 3.0 percent, to substantially cut unemployment.
"It needs to grow at something like four to four point five per cent to make really solid inroads into unemployment," Howard said in a speech to members of his Liberal Party in Victoria.
"We need to get the economy moving more rapidly to create
Australian GDP grew 3.1 percent between the December quarters of 1995 and 1996, close to the average annual rate recorded in recent decades.
Unemployment meanwhile is falling only slowly.
It reached a peak of 11 percent after the 1990-91 recession and then fell rapidly to around 8.5 percent in late 1995 before edging up again to 8.7 percent by mid 1996.

The January trend unemployment rate -- which excludes both seasonal effects and volatility -- was 8.6 percent but would have been 8.4 percent had the government statistician not recently introduced a new survey method that produces slightly different results.
Howard's predecessor as prime minister, Paul Keating, said Australia needed 4.0 percent growth.
